title: Enforce pure-kernel vs thin-CLI boundary across flagship crates (tabular, shape, rvl, pack, profile) for deterministic + wasm32 reuse
description:
## Problem
Several flagship library crates tangle pure domain compute with `std::fs::Path`, `clap`, wall clocks (`Utc::now()`), C `zstd-sys`, and ambient `~/.cmdrvl/state/witness` writes. Separating the pure deterministic kernel from the thin CLI shell guarantees reproducibility, enables in-process `cmdrvl` reuse, and unlocks zero-upload browser WASM (`cmdrvl.com/pack`, `/diff`, `/scan`).

## Scope
Coordinate and complete the pure-kernel / `fs`-free library boundary across:
- `cmdrvl/tabular` (`spine-rules/bd-nh4`: `open_bytes()` + `wasm32` check)
- `shape` (`shape/bd-8g1b`: `evaluate_bytes` + optional `cli`/`zstd` features)
- `rvl` (`rvl/bd-908`: `compare_bytes` covering numeric + overlap + `--non-numeric` + optional `cli`/`zstd` features)
- `pack` (`pack/bd-ztg`: `verify_tar_bytes`, `seal_to_tar_bytes`, in-memory `render` + optional `cli` feature)
- `profile` (in-memory `draft_bytes` / `suggest_key_bytes` over `cmdrvl_tabular::open_bytes`)
- Confirm already-clean kernels (`boundary-detectors`, `verify-core`/`verify-engine`) pass `wasm32-unknown-unknown` parity checks.
acceptance_criteria:
- All flagship domain kernels accept bytes/readers + explicit timestamps with zero `std::fs`, wall-clock, `clap`, or ambient witness access.
- `cargo check --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --no-default-features` passes across `cmdrvl-core`, `cmdrvl-tabular`, `boundary-detectors`, `shape`, `rvl`, `pack`, `profile`, and `verify-engine`.
- Golden parity test proves native CLI and in-memory library/WASM outputs match byte-for-byte.

title: Adopt fractal `control.v0` envelope, `--view brief|delta|frontier|full`, and zero-prose `refs.handoff` capsules
description:
Every workflow command in `cmdrvl` projects into the shared `evidence-protocol` `control.v0` envelope so agents use one uniform grammar from local checks up to portfolio runs.

Capabilities:
- `--view brief` (default, <= ~500 tokens): verdict, `boundary`, `coverage`, top-K `unknowns[]`, `budget`, `refs{}`, typed `next_actions[]`.
- `--view delta --since <prev_ref>` (<= ~300 tokens): turn-over-turn diff showing only newly resolved items, new regressions, remaining blockers, and budget delta.
- `--view frontier`: cursor-paginated slice of only answer-changing unknowns.
- `refs.handoff` + `cmdrvl handoff load <ref> --json`: content-addressed handoff capsule pinning inputs, boundary posture, and frontier cursor with hash drift detection for lossless multi-agent handoff after compaction.
acceptance_criteria:
- Consumes `control.v0` directly from `cmdrvl/evidence-protocol` (no forked schema).
- `--view delta --since <prev_ref>` deterministically computes resolved/regressed deltas and cuts output size >= 5x on iterative runs.
- `cmdrvl handoff load <ref>` verifies underlying input hashes and refuses with structured `E_HANDOFF_DRIFT` if inputs mutated.

title: Bootstrap cmdrvl Rust crate, CLI skeleton, spine-rules conformance, and operator.v1 manifest
description:
Stand up the `cmdrvl` binary crate (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, Rust edition 2024, clap derive CLI) with strict `spine-rules` conformance:
- Exit code trinity (`0` clean, `1` domain-negative, `2` structured refusal)
- Embedded `operator.json` (`operator.v0`) with byte-equal `--describe`, `--schema`, `--version`
- Read-only agent discovery surfaces: `--robot-triage`, `capabilities --json`, `robot-docs guide`, `doctor health --json`
- CI workflow (fmt, clippy, test) and release/Homebrew formula template matching other spine repos.
acceptance_criteria:
- `cargo test` passes including `spine-rules::golden_rules_suite!`.
- `cmdrvl --describe`, `cmdrvl --schema`, `cmdrvl capabilities --json`, `cmdrvl robot-docs guide`, and `cmdrvl --robot-triage` exit 0 with zero side effects.
notes:
2026-11-24 Alignment Note: `spine-rules` (`b18c216`) landed strict `operator.v1` (`schema_version`, `tool_version`, `commands`, `refusals`) and `cmdrvl.doctor.v1`. Target `operator.v1` and `cmdrvl.doctor.v1` directly.
2026-11-25 Plugin Dispatch Decision (Option 1): Support git/cargo-style external subcommand dispatch via clap allow_external_subcommands(true): any unknown subcommand `cmdrvl <name> [args...]` resolves `cmdrvl-<name>` on PATH (rejecting path separators or invalid names), propagates exit status verbatim, and never allows external plugins to shadow built-in subcommands. If no `cmdrvl-<name>` exists on PATH, emit a deterministic exit-2 refusal.

title: Implement `cmdrvl orient --json` & fleet doctor: one-call cold-start posture, fleet health, active state, and typed next_actions
description:
A cold agent should never run 14 experimental `--version` / `doctor` probes to understand its workspace.

Implement `cmdrvl orient --json` (read-only, bounded <= ~500 tokens by default) returning:
1. `boundary`: live posture from `veil` / `airlock` (`enforcement`, `twin_mode`, `attestation_mode`, `local_reads`, `violations`, protected path/DB roots)
2. `fleet`: installed spine binaries, semver/digests, health status, available frozen profiles, fingerprints, registries, and strategy champions
3. `active_state`: running `twinning` instances, open `canon entity` sessions, in-flight runs, and witness tail hash
4. `next_actions[]`: ranked, typed actions with `effect_class` (`pure_read | twin_exec | broker_exec | local_write | external_io | irreversible_promote`) and structured `invocation {bin, argv}`.
acceptance_criteria:
- `cmdrvl orient --json` executes read-only in <250ms, never leaks secrets, and stays within ~500 tokens in `--view brief`.
- Degrades gracefully when optional tools (`veil`, `airlock`, `twinning`, `em`) are not installed, surfacing exact install/repair `next_actions[]`.
- Integration tests cover clean workspace, missing tools, active `veil` sandbox posture, and running `twinning` instance.
notes: 2026-11-25 Plugin Discovery: `cmdrvl orient --json` should also enumerate installed external `cmdrvl-*` subcommand plugins found on PATH (name + resolved path, querying `--describe` if available) so agents see both built-in and extension commands in one call.

title: Add core invariant, property, and differential verification suites (rvl math, verify portable vs DuckDB, pack/lock fail-closed matrix)
description:
## Problem
CLI governance surfaces (`operator.v1`, `doctor.v1`) are mature, while core domain math and fail-closed invariants deserve stronger property and differential proof before building the `cmdrvl` wrapper and public browser tools on top.

## Scope
Add focused, fast invariant/property/differential test suites across core crates:
1. **`rvl`:** property tests over rounding, tie-breaking, zero-variance, NaN/Inf, overlap vs. exact alignment, and `--non-numeric` determinism.
2. **`verify`:** differential equivalence suite proving `verify-engine` (pure-Rust portable lane) and `verify-duckdb` produce identical verdicts and failure sets on all shared portable rules.
3. **`pack` & `lock`:** adversarial fail-closed test matrix (unreadable `chmod 000` files, directory/escape symlinks, `./` `CurDir` tar overwrites, truncated archives, tampered hashes).
4. **`shape` & `decoding`:** zero-overlap key-viability edge cases and independent-channel corroboration / `resolve_liveness` invariants.
acceptance_criteria:
- Property, differential, and adversarial fail-closed suites pass in CI across `rvl`, `verify`, `pack`, `lock`, `shape`, and `decoding`.
- Any discrepancy uncovered between `verify-engine` and `verify-duckdb` or in `rvl` math is fixed before wrapper implementation begins.

title: Pre-wrapper core consolidation: shared cmdrvl-core primitives, pure wasm32-clean kernels, and invariant hardening
description:
## Timing & Sequencing
Execute **after** the current P0/P1 spine sweep and messy real-world test gauntlet, and **before** implementing the `cmdrvl` porcelain wrapper (`cmd-w51` / `cmd-3w7`).

## Why
The spine tools began as independent single-purpose CLIs and grew into one system. Rather than collapsing 16 independent repos into a monorepo, this epic eliminates duplicated plumbing by construction, enforces a clean pure-kernel vs. thin-CLI separation (unlocking deterministic hashes, browser WASM, and zero-drift reuse), and hardens core domain math and fail-closed invariants before `cmdrvl` wraps the fleet.
acceptance_criteria:
- All 3 child beads closed and verified across target spine repos.
- Zero duplicated canonical-JSON / lock.v0 verification code across flagship tools.
- Core library crates compile cleanly to `wasm32-unknown-unknown --no-default-features` with byte-identical native parity.
- `cmd-3w7` (wrapper bootstrap) is cleanly unblocked to build on top of the consolidated kernels.

title: Implement `cmdrvl receipt` (atomic cancel-safe sealing), `cmdrvl twin`, and `cmdrvl sandbox --twin --egress airlock`
description:
Build the Tier 2 local orchestration layer on `asupersync`:
- `cmdrvl receipt <OLD> <NEW> --out <DIR>`: runs `vacuum`/`hashbytes`/`lock`/`shape`/`rvl`/`verify`/`assess` as a region-owned DAG with algebraic budgets and cancel-safe two-phase `pack seal` + `pack verify` (no partial packs or orphan witnesses on Ctrl-C/timeout).
- `cmdrvl twin up|status|diff|down`: ergonomic wrapper over `twinning --port 0 --overlay-of <snapshot>` projecting into `control.v0 --view brief|delta`.
- `cmdrvl sandbox [--twin] [--egress airlock] -- <agent>`: unified Tier 2 sealed workstation launcher delegating to `veil sandbox` + `airlock gate --mode policy-proxy` + `twinning`.
acceptance_criteria:
- Mid-flight cancellation during `cmdrvl receipt` drains cleanly to quiescence and leaves zero partial packs or corrupted witness lines.
- `cmdrvl twin up --port 0` emits a machine-readable readiness packet and cleans up cleanly on teardown.
- E2E integration test verifies `cmdrvl receipt` produces an offline-verifiable `pack verify` bundle.
notes:
2026-11-24 update: expose `cmdrvl report <pack>` (delegating to `pack render`) and `cmdrvl history` (delegating to `pack index`/`pack query`) for executive audit dossiers and local longitudinal pack recall.
2026-11-25 Runtime Scope Update: Do NOT mandate asupersync for cmdrvl porcelain or twinning. Keep cmdrvl lightweight and runtime-agnostic — enforce atomic, cancel-safe two-phase pack sealing (temp dir + atomic rename + clean SIGINT/timeout teardown) without pulling an unnecessary async runtime.

title: Add cross-repo E2E integration CI harness running real spine binaries on messy CSV/XLSX/Parquet fixtures
description:
## Background (Fresh-Eyes Architecture Audit)
Every `cmdrvl` repo currently tests itself in isolation with synthetic fixtures. Cross-tool seam bugs (`verify --lock` expecting `lock.input.v1`, `benchmark --lock` rejecting `blake3:`, `airlock` `messages[1].content` object format, `veil` `--explicit` flag gaps) slip past 16 green per-repo CIs.

## Scope
Add a cross-repo E2E integration harness and scheduled/workflow-dispatch GitHub Actions job in `cmdrvl/cmdrvl` that builds/installs the real spine binaries and runs the 3 canonical end-to-end pipelines on realistic messy CSV, XLSX, and Parquet fixtures:
1. **Tabular Spine Proof:** `vacuum` -> `hashbytes --algorithm blake3` -> `lock` -> `lock verify` -> `fingerprint` -> `profile` -> `shape` -> `rvl` (numeric + `--non-numeric`) -> `verify --lock` -> `assess` -> `pack seal` -> `pack verify` -> `pack render`.
2. **Boundary Plane Proof:** `veil` + `airlock` + `boundary-detectors` (verifying zero raw canary leakage across `veil`-authorized spine tools, `--explicit` flag denial, and `airlock gate` policy-proxy blocking/streaming).
3. **Twin Plane Proof:** `twinning --port 0` + `verify` + `pack seal` / `pack verify`.
acceptance_criteria:
- Runnable E2E harness script/suite executes real compiled binaries end-to-end across all 3 canonical pipelines.
- Asserts zero canary raw-cell leakage in default (redacted) outputs, `lock.v0` (`blake3:` + `sha256:`) interoperability across `lock`/`verify`/`benchmark`, and `pack verify` exit 0.
- Wired into `.github/workflows/e2e.yml` (nightly + `workflow_dispatch`).

title: Implement zero-retention local workflows: `cmdrvl inspect`, `cmdrvl diff` (shape->rvl), `cmdrvl check` (verify), and `--emit-inquiry`
description:
Provide zero-ceremony, redacted-by-default porcelain over the pure synchronous spine leaves:
- `cmdrvl inspect <FILE>` (CSV, TSV, JSONL, Parquet, XLSX): structural/schema summary without raw cell leakage.
- `cmdrvl diff <OLD> <NEW> [--key K] [--profile P]`: enforces `shape` comparability gate before `rvl`, surfaces mechanical refusal recovery (`E_NEED_KEY`), and projects into `control.v0`.
- `cmdrvl check <FILE> --rules <RULES>`: runs `verify` and projects violations into `control.v0` with `--view brief|delta`.
- `--emit-inquiry <PATH>`: escalates any local workflow cleanly into an `evidence-protocol` `inquiry.v0` for higher-order runtimes.
acceptance_criteria:
- `cmdrvl diff` refuses to run `rvl` when `shape` exits `1` (INCOMPATIBLE) and emits a structured `control.v0` verdict with `refs`.
- Default output never exposes raw cell values (`--explicit` requires explicit flag and respects `veil` boundary posture).
- `--emit-inquiry` produces schema-valid `inquiry.v0` validated against `evidence-protocol` fixtures.
notes:
2026-11-24 update: expose `cmdrvl diff --non-numeric` wiring `rvl`'s domain-agnostic non-numeric comparison mode (`date_shifts`, `categorical_transitions`, `nullity_flips`, `text_churn`, `row_churn`) into the `control.v0` brief/delta projection.
Scenario 2 friction (2026-11-25): shape and rvl do not accept composite keys via CLI flags (--key a,b or repeatable --key a --key b); composite keys currently require authoring a frozen --profile YAML. cmdrvl diff (and cmdrvl inspect) MUST accept composite keys directly on the CLI (both --key a,b and repeatable --key a --key b) and synthesize/freeze an ephemeral profile YAML under the hood (passing --profile to shape/rvl) so users and agents never have to hand-edit YAML just to diff a composite-key Parquet/CSV/XLSX table.

title: cmdrvl v0: unified porcelain CLI front door & fractal control.v0 runner
description:
Implement the unified `cmdrvl` porcelain CLI and local workflow runner specified in `docs/SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE.md`.

Goal: give AI coding agents one cold-start orientation call (`cmdrvl orient --json`), one token-bounded fractal control grammar (`control.v0` with `--view brief|delta|frontier|full`, `boundary` posture, typed `effect_class` `next_actions[]`, and `refs.handoff`), and zero-ceremony composition over the pure synchronous spine leaves (`shape`, `rvl`, `verify`, `profile`, `assess`, `pack`, `veil`, `airlock`, `twinning`), running local multi-step DAGs on Asupersync with cancel-safe two-phase sealing.
acceptance_criteria:
- All child beads closed with passing unit + integration tests and `spine-rules` conformance.
- Cold agent can orient, inspect, diff, twin-test, sandbox, and seal a receipt using one coherent CLI and `control.v0` grammar.

title: Extract shared pure-Rust cmdrvl-core crate (JCS, lock.v0, Refusal/ExitCode, and shared ordinal+HMAC Redactor)
description:
## Problem
Core primitives are currently hand-rolled and drifting across independent repos: three separate canonical-JSON serializers (`lock`, `pack`, `airlock`), divergent `lock.v0` / `blake3:` vs `sha256:` verification (`lock`, `verify`, `benchmark`, `shape`, `rvl`, `pack`), and repeated refusal/exit-code definitions.

## Scope
Create a small, zero-I/O, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, `wasm32`-clean public Rust crate (`cmdrvl/core` / `cmdrvl-core`, mirroring `cmdrvl/tabular` and `cmdrvl/boundary-detectors`) providing:
1. **RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical JSON** serializer + cross-implementation test vectors (unifying `lock`, `pack`, and `airlock/al-12z`).
2. **Canonical `blake3:` / `sha256:` hashing & `lock.v0` verification** helpers (coordinating with `spine-rules/bd-ejf`).
3. **Shared `Refusal`, `ExitCode`, and `ContractHash` types** with zero `std::fs`, zero `clap`, zero wall clock, and zero RNG.
4. Migrate `lock`, `pack`, `verify`, `benchmark`, `shape`, `rvl`, and `airlock` to consume `cmdrvl-core`.
acceptance_criteria:
- Public `cmdrvl-core` crate passes `fmt`, `clippy -D warnings`, unit/golden tests, and `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
- `lock`, `pack`, `verify`, `benchmark`, `shape`, `rvl`, and `airlock` consume shared canonical JSON & `lock.v0` verification with zero byte regression on existing fixtures.
notes: Gauntlet addition (2026-11-25): Include one shared, wasm32-clean zero-retention Redactor in cmdrvl-core supporting (1) deterministic ordinal refs by namespace (redacted:ref:k1/v1/c1) by default and (2) opt-in keyed HMAC-SHA256 (>= 16-byte key via tool env var or CMDRVL_REDACTION_KEY fallback, failing closed with E_REDACTION_KEY exit 2 on empty/short key — never silent downgrade). Eliminates the 5x redaction drift caught across verify, rvl, profile, fingerprint, and airlock during Scenarios 1-3.

comments.author: zac
comments.text:
Lane B DESIGN, PHASE 1 (posted BEFORE any code). Sources read: spine-rules docs/hashing-policy.md + src/lockfile.rs (2d1e23a); canonical JSON in lock src/lockfile/self_hash.rs (8c0cdd9), pack src/seal/manifest.rs sorted_json + witness/record.rs (e98d8bd), airlock src/hash/jcs.rs + hash.rs + fixtures/jcs (eb693d5, READ ONLY); redaction in rvl, profile (342160f), fingerprint (18d9c11), verify (0d72481), benchmark (e9c5739), decoding (cffb45a).

FINDINGS THAT SHAPE THE API:
1. Only airlock is RFC 8785. lock and pack write 'sorted compact JSON' (keys sorted by Rust String order = UTF-8/code-point order, serde_json number text) and their stored lock_hash / pack_id depend on exactly those bytes. The two differ for e.g. keys mixing U+E000..U+FFFF with U+10000+ and for floats like 1.0 / 1e21. So core ships BOTH, with names that cannot be confused; switching lock/pack to JCS would change hashes and is NOT proposed.
2. Keyed redaction has FOUR different framings: rvl = HMAC(raw bytes; row key tuples u64-LE length framed); profile + fingerprint = HMAC(kind NUL text); verify = HMAC(serde_json text of the value); benchmark = HMAC(JSON string of the cell) printed 'hmac-sha256:'+32 hex; decoding = HMAC(canonical text) printed 'hmac-sha256:'+FULL 64 hex. Prefix 'redacted:hmac-sha256:'+32 hex is shared by rvl/profile/fingerprint/verify. Ordinal letters also collide: 'k' = row key (rvl, verify) but metadata_key (fingerprint).
3. Error code drift: the bead says E_REDACTION_KEY; rvl/profile/fingerprint/benchmark/decoding use E_REDACTION_KEY_INVALID; verify uses E_REDACTION_KEY. Core will NOT hard-code a refusal code: it returns KeyError{Empty,TooShort} and each tool maps it. Please rule on one family code before migration.
4. The CMDRVL_REDACTION_KEY fallback in the bead is NEW behaviour (no tool reads it today).

CRATE: cmdrvl-core, edition 2024, MIT, #![forbid(unsafe_code)]. NO std::fs, std::env, clock, RNG, clap, threads, async. Callers pass bytes. Modules:
- jcs: to_string(&Value) -> Result<String, JcsError>; to_vec(..) -> Result<Vec<u8>, JcsError>; to_string_exact_integers(&Value) -> String (not RFC 8785 for |int| > 2^53); format_f64(f64) -> Option<String>. Semantics = airlock's jcs.rs (ported, provenance noted in the file); JcsError{pointer, number}.
- sorted_compact (the lock/pack legacy form, deliberately NOT called canonical/jcs): to_string(&Value) -> String, to_vec.
- hash: enum Algorithm{Blake3,Sha256}; Algorithm::of(prefixed)->Option (prefix only = spine-rules semantics); hash_bytes(Algorithm,&[u8]) -> String ('<alg>:<lower hex>'); parse_prefixed(&str) -> Result<(Algorithm,&str), HashError> (STRICT: known prefix + exactly 64 lowercase hex; new, stricter than any tool today, for new callers only).
- lockfile: parse(&str) -> Result<LockV0, LockRefusal>; candidates(); verify_member(&LockV0, path, bytes) -> Result<MemberVerdict, LockRefusal> = spine-rules::lockfile semantics UNCHANGED (exact path else unique basename; hash with the member's own algorithm; unknown algorithm refused; drift decided by string equality). Plus compute_lock_hash(&Value) -> String (sha256 of sorted_compact with the TOP-LEVEL lock_hash blanked, = lock's self_hash) and verify_lock_hash(&Value). run_conformance stays in spine-rules (it is test tooling); core's tests carry a COPY of its 13 cases + fixtures, marked with source commit.
- NO DEPENDENCY CYCLE: core depends on nothing from spine-rules. Later spine-rules may depend on core and re-export lockfile; the copied conformance cases are what keeps them equal until then.
- refusal: enum ExitCode{Positive=0, Negative=1, Refusal=2, Policy=3} (spine ADR); struct Refusal{code: String, message: String, detail: Value, next_command: Option<String>} and Envelope{version, outcome:'REFUSAL', refusal} with to_json() = sorted_compact (lock's to_json behaviour). Codes stay tool-owned strings.
- contract: ContractHash newtype over a strictly parsed prefixed hash, ContractHash::of_jcs(&Value) = blake3 over JCS (airlock's jcs_blake3_hash). NOTE: no tool has a ContractHash type today; this is a proposal for review, not a unification.
- redact (see byte rules below): RedactionKey::new(Vec<u8>) -> Result<_, KeyError> (empty -> Empty, <16 bytes -> TooShort; Debug prints <withheld>); RedactionKey::from_optional(Option<&[u8]>) -> Result<Option<_>>; select_key(tool_var: Option<&[u8]>, fallback: Option<&[u8]>) where a SET tool var always wins and fails closed (never falls through to the fallback, never to ordinals); constants MIN_KEY_BYTES=16, FALLBACK_ENV='CMDRVL_REDACTION_KEY' (a name only; core reads no environment); key.hmac_sha256(&[u8]) -> [u8;32]; key.marker_raw(bytes) and key.marker_tagged(tag, bytes); frame_components(parts) ; struct Namespace{tag:&'static str, letter:char} with ROW(k) VALUE(v) COLUMN(c) SHEET(s) HEADING(h) PATH(p) METADATA_KEY(k) OUTLINE(o) NAMESPACE(n); enum Scheme{Raw, Tagged}; Marker::ordinal(), Marker::keyed(&key, Scheme); mark(ns, bytes) -> String; ordinal(ns, bytes) -> usize for callers with their own text format.
EXACT BYTES: marker = 'redacted:hmac-sha256:' + lowercase hex of the FIRST 16 bytes of HMAC-SHA256(key, input). Raw: input = bytes as given (rvl: cell bytes, column-name bytes; for a row key, frame_components = for each component u64 little-endian length then the bytes, concatenated). Tagged: input = tag bytes, one 0x00, text bytes (profile 'column'; fingerprint column/sheet/heading/path/metadata_key/outline/namespace). Raw has no domain separation (rvl's documented behaviour, kept byte for byte); Tagged does. Ordinal: 'redacted:ref:<letter><n>', n from 1 per Namespace in first-appearance order, equal bytes share a ref, no hash computed. verify = Raw over serde_json text of the value. benchmark/decoding formats are reachable with hmac_sha256() + their own prefix; core adds no second marker format.

FEATURES: default = ['float-roundtrip'] which turns on serde_json/float_roundtrip (airlock requires it: serde_json's default float PARSER can be 1 ULP off, which would change a JCS hash of parsed JSON; serialization itself is unaffected). Nothing else is feature-gated; --no-default-features must build for wasm32-unknown-unknown. Caveat to document: consumers enabling serde_json/arbitrary_precision change Number semantics (untested here).

DEPENDENCIES (the ONLY five; no dev-dependencies), versions rvl's Cargo.lock resolves today: serde 1.0.228 (derive), serde_json 1.0.149, blake3 1.8.3, sha2 0.10.9, hmac 0.12.1. In Cargo.toml they will be CARET ranges ('1.0', '1.0', '1.8', '0.10', '0.12'), the committed Cargo.lock pinning exactly the versions above: EXACT '=' pins in a library would make it unusable for airlock (serde =1.0.225, serde_json =1.0.143) and pack (blake3 =1.8.2). Transitive crates come only from these five (cargo tree will be quoted).

NOT DOING in phase 1: no tool is migrated or edited; airlock is not touched; no GitHub repo (local /Users/zac/Source/cmdrvl/cmdrvl-core only); no env/file reading; no streaming hasher; no verify/benchmark/decoding adapters; no change to any hash any tool stores today.

No tool repo touched; airlock read only. No .beads in the new repo.

title: Universal "did it change?" drop-in diff mode for cmdrvl diff (multi-sheet XLSX, unlabeled prior matching, and format auto-dispatch)
description:
Add a zero-config "did it change?" drop-in workflow to `cmdrvl diff` (`cmdrvl diff <old> <new>` and `cmdrvl diff --against <lock.v0|dir> <new>`) that answers whether a newly dropped workbook, dataset, document, or folder actually changed — and where/how much — in one redacted-by-default call.

Motivated directly by pre-wrapper testing on real 50+ tab Excel workbooks with multi-row title banners, renumbered tabs, and mixed row additions where running raw per-sheet `shape`/`rvl` manually requires ~100 invocations.

4-tier deterministic fast path:
0. Byte identity (`hashbytes` BLAKE3): identical bytes return `UNCHANGED` (exit 0) immediately without parsing.
1. Container/sheet inventory & unlabeled prior matching:
   - Multi-sheet `.xlsx`/`.xls`: enumerate sheets, report added/removed tabs, and deterministically pair renumbered/renamed tabs (e.g. stripping leading numeric prefixes or matching via `fingerprint` structure).
   - Unlabeled drop-in (`--against <lock.v0|dir>`): resolve predecessor by normalized filename stem or `fingerprint` template match; refuse with typed `E_AMBIGUOUS_PREDECESSOR` + ranked candidates if ambiguous.
2. Format-aware auto-normalize & diff per changed unit:
   - Multi-sheet workbooks: auto-detect preamble rows (`fingerprint peek` -> `profile slice`), infer viable key (`profile suggest-key`), and run `shape` + `rvl --key-mode overlap --non-numeric` per tab; degrade gracefully to row/schema counts on unkeyed tabs rather than aborting the whole workbook sweep.
   - Tabular files (CSV/TSV/Parquet/JSONL): `shape` + `rvl` (numeric + `--non-numeric`).
   - Prose/HTML/Markdown/XML: dispatch to `redline` (`cmdrvl-redline` plugin) when available.
   - Directories: `vacuum` + `hashbytes` + `lock` diff, dispatching each changed file by format.
3. Compact redacted executive summary & optional sealing:
   - Headline verdict (`UNCHANGED` | `FORMATTING_ONLY` | `CHANGED` | `RESTRUCTURED`), aggregate counts (tabs/files checked, unchanged, added/removed, net row delta, schema shifts, field/text churn), and top-K changed units ranked by magnitude.
   - Strictly redacted by default (zero raw cell/prose content unless `--explicit`); supports `--sheet <name>` drill-down and `--seal` to emit a `pack verify`-clean bundle + dossier.
acceptance_criteria:
- `cmdrvl diff old.xlsx new.xlsx --json` sweeps multi-sheet workbooks with title banners, renumbered tabs, and added rows in one command without aborting the sweep on per-sheet E_ROWCOUNT/E_MIXED_TYPES.
- Identical bytes short-circuit at Tier 0 (`UNCHANGED`, exit 0) without parsing sheets.
- `--against <lock.v0|dir>` matches an unlabeled drop-in artifact to its prior version or emits typed `E_AMBIGUOUS_PREDECESSOR` with candidate list.
- Auto-dispatches tabular files to `shape`+`rvl`, prose/HTML/Markdown to `redline` (when installed), and directories via `vacuum`+`hashbytes`+`lock`.
- Default output leaks zero canary cell/prose strings; `--explicit` reveals details; `--seal` produces a `pack verify`-passing pack.
